result.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
result.summary: Frontier video generation models work in a VAE latent space that compresses video in both space and time. This compression made training tractable, but now limits high-resolution, controllable, and interactive generation -- doubling resolution quadruples token count, conditions apply to groups of frames rather than individual ones, and each response must wait for the rest of its multi-frame block. We present PixVid, a simple yet effective method that lifts a pretrained latent video model to directly generate every frame in pixel space. PixVid keeps the diffusion transformer and replaces the VAE decoder with a convolutional head that renders its outputs into pixels. We find that predicting clean video rather than velocity, together with a larger noise shift, is key to quality. Finetuned from Wan2.1-14B, PixVid is competitive with the latent baseline within $\sim 1.3$M training clips. Working framewise in pixels, it generates at $2\times$ higher resolution with the same per-frame token count, keeps depth-conditioned video editing aligned under fast motion, and responds to each action at the next frame. Project page: https://chenshuo20.github.io/PixVid/

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PixVid，将预训练的 latent 视频扩散模型迁移到像素空间：保留 diffusion transformer，用卷积头替换 VAE 解码器以直接逐帧生成像素，并指出预测干净视频而非 velocity 配合更大噪声偏移对质量关键。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文论证时空 VAE 压缩使条件只能作用于帧组、单帧响应需等待整块、token 数随分辨率急剧膨胀，这与 LVR 中 latent 瓶颈可能丢失任务必要视觉细节、证据粒度与逐帧更新延迟的问题形成可供核查的类比，可启发对表示压缩—保真度权衡与逐帧条件化的评价方式。
